title: Barclays, Citi increase stakes in iconic BlackRock fund
detail:
Barclays, Citi increase stakes in iconic BlackRock fund
Anand Sinha

BTC-USD
C
Trade BLK on Coinbase

Barclays (NYSE: BCS) and Citigroup (NYSE: C), two of the world's top banks, have increased stakes in an iconic fund launched by the world's largest asset manager, BlackRock (NYSE: BLK).

Launch in January 2024, BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (Nasdaq: IBIT) is a fund that offers indirect BTC exposure to those who want to invest in crypto from the comfort of traditional stock exchanges.

Though Bitcoin wasn't worth even $1,000 in the years following its launch in 2009, it was trading above $42,000 by the end of 2023. Though it is free from the control of centralized bodies like central banks due to its decentralized nature, Wall Street giants like BlackRock came to embrace it and launched funds tracking its spot price.

As per the onchain analytics platform SoSoValue, BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust has $64.54 billion in cumulative net inflow and $58.71 billion in net assets as of Nov. 11.

BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (Nasdaq: IBIT), Source: SoSoValue

As per Barclays's 13F filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Nov. 6, the British multinational bank held IBIT shares worth $186.66 million at the end of the third quarter of the year.

The stake is 48% higher than IBIT shares worth $88.5 million in the second quarter of 2026.

Citigroup's 13F filing on Nov. 4 shows an IBIT stake of $24.67 million in Q3 2026, up 50% from the previous quarter.

According to Bitwise, banks made up 4.9% ($258 million) of reported spot Bitcoin ETF holdings among Q3 filers so far, up from 3.2% ($107 million) in Q2.

Investment advisers led the holders with $3.5 billion in reported positions, followed by hedge fund managers ($578 million) and brokerages ($510 million).

title: Citigroup (C) Up 1.6% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
detail:
Citigroup (C) Up 1.6% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
Zacks Equity Research
Thu, November 12, 2026 at 8:30 AM MST 6 min read
C
^GSPC
Trade C on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

A month has gone by since the last earnings report for Citigroup (C). Shares have added about 1.6% in that time frame, outperforming the S&P 500.

Will the recent positive trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is Citigroup due for a pullback? Well, first let's take a quick look at the most recent earnings report in order to get a better handle on the recent catalysts for Citigroup Inc. before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late.

Citigroup Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Higher NII & Lower Expenses

Citigroup reported third-quarter 2026 earnings per share of $2.85, which surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.66. In the prior-year quarter, the company reported earnings per share of $2.24.

The company's results benefited from higher net interest income,growth across four core businesses and positive operating leverage. However, higher credit loss provisions and lower fee income acted as offsetting factors. 

Net income in the quarter was $5.25 billion, up 39.8% from the prior-year quarter.

Revenues Increase, Expenses Rise

Revenues, net of interest expenses, were $23.85 billion in the third quarter of 2026, up 7.9% year over year, marking the company's highest third-quarter revenues in a decade. The top line surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $23.66 billion.

NII increased 13.7% year over year to $16.98 billion, driven by growth in Markets, Services, Wealth and U.S. Consumer Cards.

Non-interest revenues declined 4% year over year to $6.86 billion, primarily due to weakness in Markets and U.S. Consumer Cards.

Citigroup's operating expenses declined 2.4% year over year to $13.95 billion. The decrease mainly reflected the absence of the prior-year Banamex goodwill impairment charge and lower professional services expenses. However, higher transactional and product servicing costs, deposit insurance expenses and compensation partially offset the decline.

The efficiency ratio improved to 58.5% from 64.7% in the year-ago quarter. A decline in the efficiency ratio indicates improvement in profitability.

Segmental Performance

In the Services segment, revenues were $6.61 billion, up 15% year over year. The increase reflected growth in Treasury and Trade Solutions and Securities Services.

The Markets segment's revenues increased 6% to $6.11 billion, driven by growth in Fixed Income and Equity markets revenues.

Banking revenues increased 6% to $1.74 billion, primarily driven by Investment Banking revenues, which grew 9%. Equity underwriting revenues surged 77%, while Advisory and Debt underwriting revenues declined 4% and 3%, respectively.

Citigroup, Inc. C stock is currently trading at a 12-month trailing price-to-earnings (P/E) of 9.64X, which is below the industry's 12.35X. This shows the stock is trading at a discount.

The C stock is also attractively priced compared with peers such as Bank of America BAC and Wells Fargo WFC, which are trading at higher multiples of 9.96X and 10.83X, respectively.

Citigroup's stock has appreciated 6.5% year to date, outperforming the industry's 0.6% growth. The stock has also demonstrated relative strength against its key peers, with Bank of America and Wells Fargo shares declining 7.8% and 7.9%, respectively, over the same period.

Price Performance

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

With a relatively attractive valuation and stronger share-price performance, Citigroup appears to have several factors working in its favor. But can its improving business prospects, earnings potential and ongoing strategic initiatives sustain this momentum? Let us examine whether C stock deserves a place in investors' portfolios at current levels.

Factors to Consider for Citigroup

Strategic Streamlining Efforts: C has moved closer to completing its multi-year exit from non-core international consumer banking. The sale of the Polish consumer business in June 2026 marked the final international consumer divestiture apart from remaining wind-downs of Banamex. The company also sold an additional 22.6% stake in Banamex in the second quarter after selling 25% in late 2025. The remaining Banamex deconsolidation and IPO are planned for early 2027, with management expecting the transaction to free up $5 billion in capital.

These transactions follow the completed Russia exit and divestitures of consumer franchises across Asia and EMEA. The simpler structure reduces operational complexity, releases capital and allows management to direct resources toward Services, Markets, Banking, Wealth and U.S. Consumer Cards. As the remaining divestitures and wind-downs conclude, lower stranded costs and a more focused allocation of capital should support the path toward higher sustainable returns. Backed by these initiatives, Citigroup expects revenues, excluding Legacy Franchises and reconciling items, to see a mid-single-digit compound annual growth rate (CAGR) from 2025 through 2028.

Cost Optimization Drives Sustainable Efficiency: The company continues to execute its multi-year cost-optimization strategy centered on workforce rationalization, process simplification, automation and technology investments aimed at enhancing long-term productivity and profitability.

title: As Jensen Huang leaves Nvidia, Citigroup Lowers Its Price Target on the Stock From $285 to $225. Does That Make Sense?
detail:
As Jensen Huang leaves Nvidia, Citigroup Lowers Its Price Target on the Stock From $285 to $225. Does That Make Sense?
00:00 / 00:00
Jennifer Saibil, The Motley Fool
Thu, November 12, 2026 at 9:39 AM MST 4 min read
NVDA
C
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The market is still digesting the shocking news that Jensen Huang is out as CEO of Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) after reports came out that he had two extramarital affairs and was possibly a target of Chinese spies.

Nvidia stock has fallen 14% since the news broke on Nov. 9, erasing all of the company's gains this year and more.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Wall Street is already reevaluating its price targets, and Citigroup (NYSE:C) analysts Atif Malik and Papa Sylla slashed their 12- to 18-month price target from $285 to $225, according to The Wall Street Journal.

Does this make any sense?

Image source: Nvidia.

The scandal that roiled what was the most valuable company in the world

Nvidia was the first public company to reach a $5 trillion valuation earlier this year. It has since shed more than $1 trillion of its value and trails Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) as the most valuable company in the world.

Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and shepherded it to become the most important company in the artificial intelligence (AI) economy. Reports note that he led a flat management structure with no clear successor and 60 executives reporting straight to him.

As of this writing, multiple analysts have cut their price targets for Nvidia stock, including the Citigroup team. "A leadership transition creates an overhang on the stock given his central role in strategy, product vision, customer relationships, and investor confidence," they said.

Bernstein cut its $400 price target in half, and Oppenheimer (NYSE:OPY) withdrew its price target entirely, noting that there's no clear successor in place and that some talent might leave along with Huang.

Nvidia's future is unclear

Nvidia is closely tied to Huang, and his departure is a real test for the company. However, it's still the dominant AI chipmaker, and its products are responsible for the most advanced AI development.

Sales more than doubled in the 2027 fiscal second quarter (ended July 26), and CFO and interim CEO Colette Kress has already given guidance for next year's sales to increase by 70%.

Analysts have already jumped on the news, but Nvidia's clients aren't canceling their orders, and they aren't likely to. Not only do they need Nvidia chips to keep up their pace, but Nvidia has been increasingly selling full compute systems that keep clients in its ecosystem and create high barriers to entry for competitors.

Citigroup (C) has moved to redeem all US$1.0b of its 4.150% Series Y preferred stock, retiring 1,000,000 depositary shares at US$1,000 each and ending dividend accrual on November 15, 2026.

Citigroup's move to tidy up its capital stack comes after a mixed stretch for the common stock. The 1 day share price return was 1.59% to US$124.21, but the 30 day share price return was down 5.84% and the 90 day share price return was down 10.47%. Over 1 year, total shareholder return reached 23.24%, and the 3 year total shareholder return was very large at about 20x.

Citigroup trades at a sizeable discount to both intrinsic estimates and analyst targets while retiring higher cost preferreds. Is that a margin of safety, or a warning that the market still does not buy the clean up story?

Most Popular Narrative: 18% Undervalued

Citigroup's last close of $124.21 sits well below the analyst consensus Narrative fair value of $150.71. This estimate is built using an 8.11% discount rate and detailed revenue and earnings forecasts from the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St.

Citigroup's global services franchise continues to scale, with Services revenue, net interest income, non interest revenue, deposits and assets under custody all rising at double digit rates in 2Q26. This supports further growth in fee and interest income as clients deepen their use of cash management, trade and securities services.

Still, the narrative around Citigroup can change quickly if regulatory remediation falters or if fintech and stablecoin rivals erode its transaction banking edge.

Another View: What Citigroup's P/E Is Really Saying

The first story paints Citigroup as materially undervalued versus fair value estimates. On plain earnings multiples, the picture looks more restrained. The stock trades on a P/E of 11.5x, slightly higher than the US Banks industry at 11.4x but below a fair ratio of 14.3x that the regression work points to.

That mix implies the market is giving Citigroup a small premium to the sector while still pricing it below where the fair ratio suggests the P/E could migrate. This leaves you weighing whether that discount reflects lingering business and regulatory questions or a gap that might eventually close.

CNH Industrial sits in the middle of an active debate, with price targets across the Street clustered between roughly US$11 and US$18 and an updated fair value estimate now set at US$14.70. This shift lines up with a split analyst narrative, where more bullish firms connect higher targets in the US$15 to US$18 range to their earnings assumptions, while cautious houses stay closer to US$11 to US$12 and point to execution and demand risks. As you read on, you will see how to track these moving pieces and follow the evolving CNH Industrial story.

Analyst Price Targets don't always capture the full story. Head over to our Company Report to find new ways to value CNH Industrial.

What Wall Street Has Been Saying
🐂 Bullish Takeaways

Baird, Evercore ISI, Citi, Barclays and Truist all sit in the higher price target camp for CNH Industrial, with current targets in a US$15 to US$17.50 range that reflect constructive views on execution and earnings power.

Barclays and Citi both lifted targets to US$15 after the Q3 report. They highlight improved company credibility and updated models that use a higher multiple, which feeds into the upper half of the valuation range investors are watching.

Evercore ISI and Baird use longer term agriculture recovery frameworks, including views on 2027 farm equipment demand, to support Outperform ratings and targets of US$17.50 and US$16 respectively.

🐻 Bearish Takeaways

JPMorgan keeps a more cautious stance on CNH Industrial with Underweight and Neutral ratings and targets between US$11 and US$12. The firm points to mixed demand in several end markets and ongoing cost inflation.

Across the coverage, firms such as Barclays and Truist still flag higher interest rates, margin pressures and project or demand uncertainty as key execution risks that could affect how quickly the stock closes the gap to bullish target levels.

What's in the News

CNH Industrial agreed to sell a 70% stake in its Construction Equipment business to Kobelco Construction Machinery in a joint venture that values the unit at US$1b, with CNH Industrial expecting about US$700m in cash and retaining a 30% stake.

The Kobelco transaction is expected to close by the end of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals, after which CNH Industrial would be focused on agriculture equipment, technology, and services.

CNH Industrial reported improved adjusted net income in Q3 2026 while managing challenges in EMEA and Brazil and a 6.5% decline in retail loan originations in CNH Industrial Capital that was linked to elevated delinquencies.

CNH expanded its crop residue management programme to 25 locations across 11 states and opened a parts warehouse in Ludhiana, while also planning a software update rollout from Q4 2026 through 2027 to align emissions system controls with updated U.S. Environmental Protection Agency guidance.

title: 69% Upside for Affirm? Citi Thinks So, and Here’s How
detail:
69% Upside for Affirm? Citi Thinks So, and Here’s How
David Hanson

Trading disclosure
69% Upside for Affirm? Citi Thinks So, and Here's How ©@Przemek Klos from Przemek Klos via Canva, @tanaonte via Canva
Key Takeaways

Affirm is down 23% from its July high after a quarter of fast growth and higher late payments. Citi kept its Buy rating and its $115 target, 69% above today's price.

Citi's case rests on three things: volume growth above guidance, new partners that bring in more merchants, and funding costs Affirm can absorb. The September quarter supported most of it.

Citi's $115 target is 27x the earnings analysts expect over the next twelve months. That's close to the 28x Affirm has averaged since its forward P/E turned positive in 2024.

The call looks right as long as delinquencies settle after the holidays. Affirm reports that quarter in early February.

Affirm Holdings (AFRM:NASDAQ) just grew its volume 34%, and the stock is still down 23% from its July high. Citi's Bryan Keane reiterated his Buy rating and $115 price target on Nov. 11, 69% above today's price.

A strong quarter with a credit wrinkle

Affirm's fiscal first-quarter results, out Nov. 5, beat its own guidance: gross merchandise volume (GMV) rose 34% to $14.4 billion, and revenue rose 35% to $1.26 billion.

But 30-day-plus delinquencies on its monthly loans rose 35 basis points from the June quarter to 2.9%. CFO Rob O'Hare said on the call that Affirm chose to "run some experiments within the approvals and the origination" in September. Affirm also guided its December-quarter GAAP operating margin below what analysts expected, on higher warrant expense for a large partner signing up new users.

TIKR tracks 36 analysts on Affirm. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Affirm, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Affirm's Analyst Ratings

How Citi gets to $115

Keane laid out his case in an early-October note, and Affirm delivered on most of it.

He expected GMV growth at the high end of management's 27% to 30% outlook. Affirm grew 34%, and O'Hare said the business is "growing at a high 30s rate today."

He also pointed to early-stage partnerships with Intuit's QuickBooks, ServiceTitan and Amazon in the UK. CEO Max Levchin said on the call that services, the category those software partners feed, was the best performer of the categories Affirm breaks out.

And he put the hit from recent rate moves at 15 to 20 basis points of revenue less transaction costs (RLTC). Funding costs rose 27 basis points from the June quarter, yet RLTC came in at 4.3% of GMV, above management's 3.75% to 4% medium-term range.

Key Takeaways

Lucid Group stock is down 78% over the past year, and on Nov. 11 Citi cut its price target to $9 from $11 and kept its Buy rating.

Citi's $9 is 138% above today's price and 37% above the $7 consensus target, which has fallen from about $24 a year ago.

The target asks for just 1.5x forward sales, but about $4.9 billion of debt and loans and $3.07 billion of preferred stock rank ahead of common shareholders.

Lucid is unlikely to reach $9 in the next year, and full-year results in late February, with 2027 guidance, are the next test.

Lucid Group (LCID:NASDAQ) has lost 78% of its value over the past year, and analysts spent this week cutting their targets after its third-quarter report. Citi's new $9 target still sits 138% above today's price of $3.78.

Fewer cars, more borrowing

Lucid delivered 3,806 vehicles in the third quarter, down 7% from a year earlier, as the US electric-vehicle market shrank 41% after federal EV tax credits ended. Free cash flow improved 30% from the second quarter but was still -$1.04 billion. So Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF), Lucid's largest investor, added $1.75 billion to its loan, which Lucid says funds it into the fourth quarter of 2027.

Citi still says Buy

Citi analyst Michael Ward kept his Buy rating on Nov. 11 and cut his target to $9 from $11, pointing to the improved cash burn. It's his third cut since he initiated coverage at $17 in March. The biggest launch he was counting on, Midsize, Lucid's lower-priced platform, has since slipped from a late-2026 start to production in the second half of 2027.

The sales math is the easy part

The average target from the 11 analysts covering Lucid has fallen from about $24 a year ago to $7, which is still 74% above the price. This chart tracks the consensus target over the past year.

Lucid Group (LCID): analysts' consensus (mean) price target, $ per share, last year (TIKR)

Those targets depend on a steep climb in sales. Analysts expect revenue to more than double in 2027, to $3.32 billion, and to double again in 2028, to $6.71 billion.

Lucid Group (LCID): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2024-2028 (TIKR)

That's a lot to ask of a car that isn't due to start production until the second half of 2027. But if analysts are right, $9 is just 1.5x the sales they expect per share over the next twelve months. Lucid trades at 0.6x, near its five-year low, against a five-year average of 10x.
